articleTitle: Three Hacktron Researchers Used Anthropic’s Claude to Break into OpenAI in Under 72 Hours

sources.title: Security researchers used Claude to help them hack into OpenAI

claims.claim: A trio of security researchers from Hacktron announced that they had breached OpenAI employee accounts in less than 72 hours.

claims.evidence: A team of three independent security researchers at Hacktron says it took less than 72 hours for them to hack into OpenAI employee accounts using Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 and 5, The Wall Street Journal reports.

editorial.claim: It also highlights the importance of securing image‑processing pipelines, especially in third‑party services that handle user uploads.
Readers should note that the researchers did not access the internal code of OpenAI’s Monorepo; they only demonstrated that they could gain access to employee accounts and submit a pull request.

The incident also illustrates the potential for AI tools to accelerate vulnerability exploitation, a development that may prompt tighter controls on how such models are deployed and accessed by developers and researchers alike.
